clues: This old village in Russia sits on the bank of the Don River. It lies upstream from a big port city.
Spring floods sank this small town time and time again. So the Cossacks moved their capital to high ground.
For close to two hundred years, this was the heart of Don Cossack life. It was their seat of rule and their capital town.
Its old church, done in 1719, holds a famed screen of holy pictures. The screen is carved wood with gold on it.
More than forty old sites of note crowd this small village. They lie in it and all round it too.
